- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid false optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to overestimate — apply a 3–5% downward bias to the final 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model often misreads trend direction — use a 2–3 day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by >5% in early days of the horizon, reduce initial forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion behavior.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive, apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid overestimating price persistence.
